title: Early and Late Renewals in Noticed C&I Termination Damages
content:
**§ Noticed terminations: renewal history** - Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts

The damages rate of a noticed termination is scaled by the contract's renewal history: a contract whose current term began through a renewal signed 60 days or more before the term start date scales it by 0.90, a contract whose current term began through a renewal signed fewer days before the term start date scales it by 0.95, and a contract never renewed leaves it unscaled. Scaling multiplies the damages rate per kWh by the figure shown.

The renewal signed date and the term start date are read from the contract record; a contract with no renewal signed date has never been renewed. The days are calendar days from the renewal signed date to the term start date, the signing day not counted.

| Contract record | Damages rate multiplied by |
|---|---|
| renewal signed 60 days or more before the term start date | 0.90 |
| renewal signed 0 to 59 days before the term start date | 0.95 |
| no renewal signed date | 1, unscaled |

## Cases (hypothetical dates)

- Renewal signed 3 July 2026 for a term starting 1 September 2026: 60 days, scaled by 0.90.
- Renewal signed 4 July 2026 for the same term start: 59 days, scaled by 0.95.
- Renewal signed during holdover on 10 November 2026, the new term starting on the next scheduled meter read of 3 December 2026: 23 days, scaled by 0.95.
- A contract still in the term it was first executed for: unscaled.
